## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the journey, the preparations, those who stayed behind and the three. None is used in this draft.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Tabuk, the Byzantines, and the date and route of the journey; the inventory title itself says the identification is from later tradition.
- Not drafted: 9:40 (told in the draft for the emigration), 9:43-59 (the leave given, and the hypocrites' excuses, offerings and complaints), 9:84-85 and 9:94-96; these are for a later pass.
- 9:43 addresses the Prophet about leave given to those who stayed behind; it needs a scholar's wording before it is drafted and is left out for that reason.
- The ayat give no numbers, no dates and no commanders; none are given in this draft.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The call to go out  (`#the-call-to-go-out`)

Cited ayat: 9:38-39, 9:41-42

> **9:38** يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَا لَكُمْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمُ ٱنفِرُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ أَرَضِيتُم بِٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا مِنَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ فَمَا مَتَٰعُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ
>
> **9:39** إِلَّا تَنفِرُوا۟ يُعَذِّبْكُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا وَيَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْمًا غَيْرَكُمْ وَلَا تَضُرُّوهُ شَيْـًٔا وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

> **9:41** ٱنفِرُوا۟ خِفَافًا وَثِقَالًا وَجَٰهِدُوا۟ بِأَمْوَٰلِكُمْ وَأَنفُسِكُمْ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
>
> **9:42** لَوْ كَانَ عَرَضًا قَرِيبًا وَسَفَرًا قَاصِدًا لَّٱتَّبَعُوكَ وَلَٰكِنۢ بَعُدَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلشُّقَّةُ وَسَيَحْلِفُونَ بِٱللَّهِ لَوِ ٱسْتَطَعْنَا لَخَرَجْنَا مَعَكُمْ يُهْلِكُونَ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنَّهُمْ لَكَٰذِبُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (9:38): The believers were asked what was wrong with them that when they were told to go out in God's way they clung heavily to the earth, and whether they were content with the life of this world instead of the Hereafter; the enjoyment of this life in the Hereafter is little.

**c2** (9:39): If they did not go out, God would punish them with a painful punishment and replace them with another people, and they would not harm Him at all; God has power over all things.

**c3** (9:41): They were told to go out, light and heavy, and to strive with their wealth and themselves in God's way; that is better for them, if they only knew.

**c4** (9:42): Had it been a near gain and an easy journey, they would have followed you, but the distance seemed far to them; they will swear by God that, had they been able, they would have gone out with you, destroying themselves, and God knows that they are liars.

### One-minute summary

The believers were asked why they clung heavily to the earth when told to go out in God's way, and warned of a painful punishment and replacement if they did not go [c1][c2]. They were told to go out, light and heavy, and to strive with their wealth and themselves, and the ayat say that some would swear they could not [c3][c4].

### Complete story

The believers were asked what was wrong with them that when they were told to go out in God's way they clung heavily to the earth [c1]. They were asked whether they were content with the life of this world instead of the Hereafter; the enjoyment of this life in the Hereafter is little [c1].

If they did not go out, God would punish them with a painful punishment and replace them with another people, and they would not harm Him at all; God has power over all things [c2].

They were told to go out, light and heavy, and to strive with their wealth and themselves in God's way; that is better for them, if they only knew [c3]. Had it been a near gain and an easy journey, they would have followed you, but the distance seemed far to them [c4]. They will swear by God that, had they been able, they would have gone out with you, destroying themselves, and God knows that they are liars [c4].

### Deep study

The ayat move from a question to a warning and then to a command, and end with a description of those who give excuses [c1][c2][c3][c4]. The phrase light and heavy is read in more than one way and is left as it stands [c3].

### Kids mode

The believers were told to go out in God's way, and some held back [c1]. The ayat say that going out and striving is better for them, if they knew [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat set the enjoyment of this life beside the Hereafter [c1]. Another is that the ayat describe excuses as sworn by those who did not go [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: where the believers were told to go, against whom, when, or how far the distance was; the ayat name no place or enemy.
- Not established: who the ones who swore were, or how many.
- Not established: what the light and heavy refer to; commentators read the phrase in more than one way.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name Tabuk, the opponents and the place and the season of the journey. The detailed accounts rest on biographical and historical sources (sira) and on later reports that the repository does not yet hold.

## 2. Those who stayed behind, and those excused  (`#those-who-stayed-behind`)

Cited ayat: 9:81-83, 9:86-93

> **9:81** فَرِحَ ٱلْمُخَلَّفُونَ بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ خِلَٰفَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ وَكَرِهُوٓا۟ أَن يُجَٰهِدُوا۟ بِأَمْوَٰلِهِمْ وَأَنفُسِهِمْ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَقَالُوا۟ لَا تَنفِرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْحَرِّ قُلْ نَارُ جَهَنَّمَ أَشَدُّ حَرًّا لَّوْ كَانُوا۟ يَفْقَهُونَ
>
> **9:82** فَلْيَضْحَكُوا۟ قَلِيلًا وَلْيَبْكُوا۟ كَثِيرًا جَزَآءًۢ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
>
> **9:83** فَإِن رَّجَعَكَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَىٰ طَآئِفَةٍ مِّنْهُمْ فَٱسْتَـْٔذَنُوكَ لِلْخُرُوجِ فَقُل لَّن تَخْرُجُوا۟ مَعِىَ أَبَدًا وَلَن تُقَٰتِلُوا۟ مَعِىَ عَدُوًّا إِنَّكُمْ رَضِيتُم بِٱلْقُعُودِ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ فَٱقْعُدُوا۟ مَعَ ٱلْخَٰلِفِينَ

> **9:86** وَإِذَآ أُنزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ أَنْ ءَامِنُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ وَجَٰهِدُوا۟ مَعَ رَسُولِهِ ٱسْتَـْٔذَنَكَ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلطَّوْلِ مِنْهُمْ وَقَالُوا۟ ذَرْنَا نَكُن مَّعَ ٱلْقَٰعِدِينَ
>
> **9:87** رَضُوا۟ بِأَن يَكُونُوا۟ مَعَ ٱلْخَوَالِفِ وَطُبِعَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ
>
> **9:88** لَٰكِنِ ٱلرَّسُولُ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ جَٰهَدُوا۟ بِأَمْوَٰلِهِمْ وَأَنفُسِهِمْ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتُ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ
>
> **9:89** أَعَدَّ ٱللَّهُ لَهُمْ جَنَّٰتٍ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
>
> **9:90** وَجَآءَ ٱلْمُعَذِّرُونَ مِنَ ٱلْأَعْرَابِ لِيُؤْذَنَ لَهُمْ وَقَعَدَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ سَيُصِيبُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
>
> **9:91** لَّيْسَ عَلَى ٱلضُّعَفَآءِ وَلَا عَلَى ٱلْمَرْضَىٰ وَلَا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ مَا يُنفِقُونَ حَرَجٌ إِذَا نَصَحُوا۟ لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ مَا عَلَى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ مِن سَبِيلٍ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
>
> **9:92** وَلَا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا مَآ أَتَوْكَ لِتَحْمِلَهُمْ قُلْتَ لَآ أَجِدُ مَآ أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ تَوَلَّوا۟ وَّأَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ ٱلدَّمْعِ حَزَنًا أَلَّا يَجِدُوا۟ مَا يُنفِقُونَ
>
> **9:93** إِنَّمَا ٱلسَّبِيلُ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَـْٔذِنُونَكَ وَهُمْ أَغْنِيَآءُ رَضُوا۟ بِأَن يَكُونُوا۟ مَعَ ٱلْخَوَالِفِ وَطَبَعَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (9:81): Those who were left behind rejoiced at staying behind the Messenger of God and disliked to strive with their wealth and themselves in God's way; they said: do not go out in the heat; they were told that the Fire of Hell is hotter, if they understood.

**c2** (9:82): Let them laugh a little and weep much, as recompense for what they used to earn.

**c3** (9:83): If God brought the Messenger back to a party of them and they asked leave to go out, he was to say: you will never go out with me and will never fight an enemy with me; you were content to sit the first time, so sit with those who stay behind.

**c4** (9:86-87): When a surah was sent down telling them to believe in God and to strive with His Messenger, those of them with means asked leave and said: leave us to be with those who sit; they were content to be with those who stay behind, and their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand.

**c5** (9:88-89): But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and themselves; for them are the good things, and they are the successful; God has prepared for them gardens with rivers beneath them, abiding there; that is the great triumph.

**c6** (9:90): The excuse-makers among the desert nomads came to be given leave, and those who lied to God and His Messenger stayed behind; a painful punishment will strike those of them who disbelieve.

**c7** (9:91): There is no blame on the weak, the sick, or those who find nothing to spend, if they are sincere to God and His Messenger; there is no way against those who do good; God is Forgiving, Merciful.

**c8** (9:92): There is no blame either on those who came to him for mounts, and he said that he found nothing to carry them on; they turned away with tears flowing from sorrow that they could not find anything to spend.

**c9** (9:93): The blame is only on those who ask leave while they are rich, content to be with those who stay behind; God has sealed their hearts, so they do not know.

### One-minute summary

The ayat say that those who were left behind rejoiced at staying behind the Messenger of God, and that those of them with means asked leave to sit [c1][c4]. They say that there is no blame on the weak, the sick and those who find nothing to spend, and that the Messenger and those with him strove [c5][c7].

### Complete story

Those who were left behind rejoiced at staying behind the Messenger of God and disliked to strive with their wealth and themselves in God's way [c1]. They said: do not go out in the heat; they were told that the Fire of Hell is hotter, if they understood [c1]. Let them laugh a little and weep much, as recompense for what they used to earn [c2].

If God brought the Messenger back to a party of them and they asked leave to go out, he was to say: you will never go out with me and will never fight an enemy with me; you were content to sit the first time, so sit with those who stay behind [c3]. When a surah was sent down telling them to believe in God and to strive with His Messenger, those of them with means asked leave and said: leave us to be with those who sit; their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand [c4].

But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and themselves; for them are the good things, and they are the successful; God has prepared for them gardens with rivers beneath them, abiding there; that is the great triumph [c5]. The excuse-makers among the desert nomads came to be given leave, and those who lied to God and His Messenger stayed behind; a painful punishment will strike those of them who disbelieve [c6].

There is no blame on the weak, the sick, or those who find nothing to spend, if they are sincere to God and His Messenger; there is no way against those who do good; God is Forgiving, Merciful [c7]. There is no blame either on those who came to him for mounts, and he said that he found nothing to carry them on; they turned away with tears flowing from sorrow that they could not find anything to spend [c8]. The blame is only on those who ask leave while they are rich, content to be with those who stay behind; God has sealed their hearts, so they do not know [c9].

### Deep study

The ayat separate those who stayed behind by reason: some are condemned for choosing to sit, and others are cleared because they could not go [c4][c7][c8][c9]. The ayah on the Fire of Hell answers the excuse about the heat with a comparison [c1]. The ayat that describe the Messenger and those who believed with him say what is prepared for them [c5].

### Kids mode

Some people stayed behind and were glad, saying the heat was too great [c1]. The ayat say that the weak and the sick and those who had nothing to spend are not to blame [c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat tell apart those who chose to sit from those who could not go and were sorry about it [c7][c8][c9]. Another is that the ayat set the excuse of the heat beside the Fire of Hell [c1].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who stayed behind by name or how many; the ayat describe them and do not name them.
- Not established: when the surah was sent down that called them to believe and strive, or which surah is meant.
- Not established: how the Messenger answered those who came for mounts beyond the words the ayah records.
- Not established: what the day of the return to a party of them was.

## 3. The three who were left behind  (`#the-three-who-were-left-behind`)

Cited ayat: 9:117-118

> **9:117** لَّقَد تَّابَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِىِّ وَٱلْمُهَٰجِرِينَ وَٱلْأَنصَارِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُ فِى سَاعَةِ ٱلْعُسْرَةِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا كَادَ يَزِيغُ قُلُوبُ فَرِيقٍ مِّنْهُمْ ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِنَّهُۥ بِهِمْ رَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ
>
> **9:118** وَعَلَى ٱلثَّلَٰثَةِ ٱلَّذِينَ خُلِّفُوا۟ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا ضَاقَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْأَرْضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتْ وَضَاقَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ أَنفُسُهُمْ وَظَنُّوٓا۟ أَن لَّا مَلْجَأَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّآ إِلَيْهِ ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيْهِمْ لِيَتُوبُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

### Claims

**c1** (9:117): God turned in mercy to the Prophet and the emigrants and the helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a party of them had almost swerved; then He turned to them; He is compassionate and merciful to them.

**c2** (9:118): God turned also to the three who were left behind, until the earth, for all its breadth, closed in on them and their own souls closed in on them and they realised that there is no refuge from God except in Him; then He turned to them so that they might turn; God is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.

### One-minute summary

The ayat say that God turned in mercy to the Prophet and the emigrants and the helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship [c1]. They say that God turned also to the three who were left behind, until the earth closed in on them, and that He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful [c2].

### Complete story

God turned in mercy to the Prophet and the emigrants and the helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a party of them had almost swerved [c1]. Then He turned to them; He is compassionate and merciful to them [c1].

God turned also to the three who were left behind, until the earth, for all its breadth, closed in on them and their own souls closed in on them [c2]. They realised that there is no refuge from God except in Him; then He turned to them so that they might turn; God is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful [c2].

### Deep study

The ayat name the hour of hardship and say the hearts of a party almost swerved before God turned to them [c1]. The three who were left behind are given a short account of their distress: the earth closing in, their own souls closing in, and the realisation that refuge is only with God [c2].

### Kids mode

God turned in mercy to the Prophet and the believers in a time of hardship [c1]. He also turned to three who had been left behind, when the earth felt too small for them [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat tie the hour of hardship to God's turning in mercy [c1]. Another is that the three found that there is no refuge from God except in Him, and God turned to them so that they might turn [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the three were by name, why they were left behind, or how long it lasted.
- Not established: what the hour of hardship was or how long it was; the ayah names it as the hour of hardship.
- Not established: whose hearts almost swerved, or why.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names of the three and the details of their story.
